common_name: Maui Gold Elephant Ear (Bright Chartreuse-Gold Sun-Tolerant Colocasia)

planting.note: Plant divisions or corms after all frost danger has passed when soil is warm; Maui Gold is a bright chartreuse-gold elephant ear noted for tolerating more direct sun than most colocasia without leaf scorch, provided soil stays consistently moist.

directions: Plant divisions or corms in rich, consistently moist to wet soil in partial shade to full sun, watering generously since colocasia is highly moisture-demanding during active growth, especially in brighter light. Maui Gold produces broad, heart-shaped leaves in a vivid chartreuse to golden-yellow color that intensifies with more sun exposure, unlike many darker-leaved colocasia cultivars that prefer shade, making it a bright focal point for a sunny bog garden, pond edge, or large container. It grows quickly through the warm season, reaching full size by midsummer from a spring planting. In zone 8-10 gardens the corms often survive in the ground through mild winters with heavy mulching; in colder zones, dig and store corms in frost-free conditions over winter.

common_name: Regal Shields Elephant Ear (Giant Silvery-Blue Purple-Veined Colocasia)

planting.note: Plant divisions after all frost danger has passed when soil is warm; Regal Shields, a Plant Delights Nursery introduction, forms enormous silvery-blue-gray leaves with dark purple veining on a giant Colocasia gigantea plant.

directions: Plant divisions in rich, consistently moist to wet soil in partial shade, giving this giant selection plenty of room to reach its full, dramatic size. Regal Shields, a Plant Delights Nursery introduction of Colocasia gigantea, produces enormous, thick, silvery-blue-gray leaves several feet long with striking dark purple veining, one of the boldest and most architectural foliage plants available for a large shade or partial-shade planting, pond margin, or tropical-style border. Unlike many colocasia, gigantea types also produce fragrant flowers in summer that some gardeners specifically grow the species for. Water generously, since colocasia is highly moisture-demanding, and in zone 8-10 gardens the large tuberous rootstock often survives in the ground through mild winters with heavy mulching; in colder zones, dig and store indoors over winter.

common_name: Siam Ruby Banana (Striking Red-and-Green Striped Ornamental Banana)

planting.note: Plant container or divided pups after all frost danger has passed in rich, moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Siam Ruby is grown chiefly as a dramatic ornamental foliage banana for its vivid red-and-green striped leaves rather than for reliable fruit production outside true tropical climates.

directions: Plant in rich, moist, well-drained soil in full sun, watering generously and feeding regularly through the growing season to support the fast, lush growth typical of ornamental bananas. Siam Ruby is prized above all for its spectacular foliage, with broad leaves striped and mottled in deep wine-red over green in an ever-shifting pattern that makes it one of the showiest tropical-look foliage plants for a Gulf South summer landscape, whether in a large container or planted directly in a bed. While it can produce small bananas in long, warm growing seasons, it is grown primarily as an ornamental rather than for reliable fruit in most of its hardiness range. In zone 8-9 gardens the top growth is usually killed by winter frost but the underground rhizome often survives with heavy mulching, resprouting in spring; in colder areas, dig and overwinter indoors or grow in a large movable container.
